'''''Malva moschata''''', the '''musk mallow''' or '''musk-mallow''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[family (botany)|family]] Malvaceae. It is a [[herbaceous plant]] producing pink, five-petaled flowers in summer. It is native to Eurasia and has been introduced elsewhere, being cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]].

== Description ==
The [[perennial]] plant grows up to {{convert|60|cm}} tall. It has hairy stems and foliage. The [[leaves]] are alternate, {{Convert|2–8|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}} long and broad, palmately lobed with five to seven lobes. The basal leaves are very shallowly lobed, while those higher on the stems are deeply divided, with narrow, acuminate lobes.

Blooming in summer, flowers appear in clusters in the leaf axils, each flower {{Convert|3.2–5|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}} in diameter, with five bright pink petals that have a truncated to notched apex; they have a distinctive musky odour. The fruit is a disc-shaped [[schizocarp]] {{Convert|3–6|mm|frac=16}} in diameter, containing 10–16 seeds, the seeds individually enclosed in a [[mericarp]] covered in whitish hairs. It has a [[chromosome]] count of 2''n''=42.<ref name="fnwe">Flora of NW Europe: [http://ip30.eti.uva.nl/BIS/flora.php?selected=beschrijving&menuentry=soorten&id=2136 ''Malva moschata'']{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="blamey">Blamey, M. & Grey-Wilson, C. (1989). ''Flora of Britain and Northern Europe''. {{ISBN|0-340-40170-2}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
[[File:Malva moschata 021.jpg|thumb|[[Deschambault-Grondines]], Quebec, Canada]]

The species is native to Europe and southwestern Asia, from [[Spain]] north to the [[British Isles]] and [[Poland]], and east to southern [[Russia]] and [[Turkey]].<ref name="fe">Flora Europaea: [http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/cgi-bin/nph-readbtree.pl/feout?FAMILY_XREF=&GENUS_XREF=Malva&SPECIES_XREF=moschata&TAXON_NAME_XREF=&RANK= ''Malva moschata'']</ref><ref name="mc">Med-Checklist: [http://ww2.bgbm.org/mcl/PTaxonDetail.asp?NameId=15298&PTRefFk=1276 ''Malva moschata'']</ref><ref name="fnwe" /><ref name="blamey" /> 

It has been introduced to and become [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] in several areas with temperate climates away from its native range, including Scandinavia, New Zealand, and North America.<ref name="blamey" /><ref name="rhs" /><ref name="mp" />

== Ecology ==
It occurs on dry, but fertile soils at altitudes from sea level up to {{convert|1500|m|abbr=on}}. Natural [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] with the closely related ''[[Malva alcea]]'' are occasionally found.<ref name=blamey />

The flowers are usually pollinated by bees.<ref name="blamey" />

[[File:White musk mallow in Tuntorp 2.jpg|thumb|upright=.9|'Alba' with white flowers]]
== Uses ==

''Malva moschata'' is widely grown as an [[ornamental plant]] for its attractive scented flowers, produced for a long period through the summer. Several [[cultivar]]s have been selected for variation in flower colour, including 'Rosea' with dark pink flowers.<ref name=rhs>Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''. Macmillan {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}.</ref><ref name=mp>Malva Pages: [http://www.malvaceae.info/Genera/Malva/Bismalva.php Musk Mallows (section Bismalva)]</ref> <!-- AGM withdrawn The cultivar 'Alba' (white flowered) has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector – ''Malva moschata'' f. ''alba''|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=5531|accessdate=19 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants – Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 63 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 25 March 2018}}</ref>-->

The leaves and flowers can be added to salads. The seeds are also edible.{{Citation needed|date=February 2026}}
